extracted.intended_audience: editors, authors, and educated general readers interested in scientific and literary books (readers of Popular Science Monthly); also professional readers (physicians, scientists) where noted
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluative guidance and implicit criteria (from book reviews) for what makes effective popular-science, scientific, medical, historical/memorial, and literary works — addressing audience, scope, evidence, style, structure, and trustworthiness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Utility and practical value of philosophical/systematic work
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognition of the great value of knowledge for useful ends; the philosophy should be 'animated by a grand utility' and bear upon 'the regulation of human conduct' and the advancement of human welfare.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A philosophical system is credited when it supplies scientific knowledge of nature and human nature that is valuable as guidance for individuals and society, links theoretical principles to ethical/political consequences, and prepares for intellectual or social emergencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Philosophy as foundation for ethics
rubrics_metrics.description: Divisions of a system (First Principles, Biology, Psychology, Sociology) should serve as foundations for an ultimate exposition of 'Principles of Ethics' and determine right and wrong of human actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the work connects scientific laws and principles to moral questions and whether its parts cohere toward ethical conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate audience targeting for popular-science books
rubrics_metrics.description: Write 'neither for scientific readers as such, nor... for the masses, but for that large class... who, without being engaged in scientific pursuits, yet have sufficient education and intelligence to be interested ... when presented in an untechnical manner.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim tone and depth at educated non-specialists: enough precision for understanding principles and methods without requiring mastery of technical details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance of precision and accessibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Present material 'in language and manner as unprofessional as is consistent with precision'; keep statements plain, direct, clear, and condensed while remaining ample for purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid excessive technicality or excessive popularization; maintain precision but use untechnical language where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish between the certain and the conjectural
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep distinct the line between the certain and the conjectural, and indicate as far as possible the degree of confidence to be placed in data and conclusions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly mark which claims are established versus tentative; provide readers guidance on confidence levels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compactness and trustworthiness for general reference
rubrics_metrics.description: A needed popular work should be 'compact in form, and thoroughly trustworthy for reading and reference' — not overly large or crowding with secondary material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize concise, well-selected material suitable for both reading and reference rather than exhaustive professional treatises or overly superficial popularizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure: systematic coverage and useful chapter topics
rubrics_metrics.description: Good popular-science works organize systematic discussion (e.g., introduction on relation to life, chapters on distance/dimensions, methods and apparatus, specific phenomena, and a concluding summary of facts).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a clear, logical chapter structure that moves from fundamentals to methods to specific phenomena, ending with synthesis or summary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of illustrations and expert appendices
rubrics_metrics.description: Include numerous illustrations and, when useful, appendices or contributions from other experts to present important views (e.g., Professor Langley's appendix on light and heat).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support textual claims with figures/plates and authoritative supplementary material when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid rhetorical flourish in favor of substantive exposition
rubrics_metrics.description: The reviewer praises a book that 'trusts the grandeur of his theme to kindle interest' rather than relying on rhetoric; statements should be plain and factual.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize clear exposition of facts and explanations over rhetorical embellishment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope-limitation aligned with policy relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: When addressing social/political questions (e.g., Chinese immigration), limit treatment to aspects 'likely to determine the legislative action of the country' and clearly delineate what is outside scope (political/commercial issues reserved for future work).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define and keep to a scope appropriate to the work's aims; do not mix in unrelated philosophical issues unless intended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of empirical evidence and careful statistical study
rubrics_metrics.description: Conclusions about social questions should be based on careful study of available data (customs statistics of arrivals and departures, census) and testimony from investigations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support assertions with empirical data and documented evidence; cite primary sources and official statistics where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temperateness and even-handedness of treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: A valuable treatment of contentious issues is 'full, intelligent, and temperate' rather than inflammatory or partisan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt measured, evidence-based tone, especially on divisive subjects, to increase credibility and utility for policy discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity about special-community characteristics and social interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize and explain cultural or social conservatism in studied communities (e.g., Chinese conservatism as adjustment to environment) without overreaching into speculative judgments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide balanced cultural interpretation grounded in observed behavior and social context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Medical/professional texts: basis in latest science and clinical practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Medical volumes should be 'based upon the latest scientific knowledge brought to the test of practice' and written from an appropriate professional standpoint (e.g., physiological).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure medical claims reflect current physiology/animal chemistry and are connected to clinical or practical experience; include history, mechanisms, and treatment chapters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Medical text accessibility to non-professionals
rubrics_metrics.description: Although aimed at physicians, valuable medical works can also be instructive to non-professional readers of ordinary intelligence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write with enough clarity and explanation that educated lay readers can learn practical, useful information, while retaining professional rigor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of quackish misinformation
rubrics_metrics.description: Warns against abundance of quackish books; legitimate works should correct public ignorance and not mislead.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish scientifically grounded treatments from popular quackery; emphasize evidence-based recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thorough, candid institutional/memorial histories
rubrics_metrics.description: A worthy memorial or institutional history should record year-by-year activities with minuteness (gifts, troubles, resolutions) and candidly set forth mistakes as lessons for other bodies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include detailed annals, notices of members, portraits, and special papers; candidness about difficulties is valuable management guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of diverse scholarly contributions
rubrics_metrics.description: Memorial volumes are strengthened by including a range of special scientific papers across topics and by reproducing addresses and proceedings related to the subject (e.g., multiple addresses on Joseph Henry).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect essays/papers/addresses from varied specialists to create a comprehensive volume that documents contributions and perspectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Usefulness of practical educational initiatives
rubrics_metrics.description: The institution's practical scientific lectures to teachers with object-illustrations are highlighted as important — practical outreach to improve instruction is a mark of value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize and document practical educational programs and their objectives/outcomes in institutional reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelistic balance between didacticism and narrative
rubrics_metrics.description: A novel that is 'of too didactic a quality' may fail popularly; moralizing and preachiness can hinder reception even if intellectually valuable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance moral or didactic discussions with compelling plot and character development; use critical feedback to improve.

rubrics_metrics.name: Empirical field investigation for practical hazard studies
rubrics_metrics.description: Works investigating practical hazards (e.g., sewer-gas and house-drainage) should result from impartial local investigations and document the prevalence and variety of defects discovered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Base practical-safety recommendations on systematic, impartial local inquiry and clearly report observed defects and remedies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support controversial archaeological claims with illustrations and comparisons
rubrics_metrics.description: When asserting discovery (e.g., Paleolithic implements in Egypt), present typological comparisons and numerous illustrations (plates) to substantiate the claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide photographic/illustrative evidence and comparative typology; reference prior published remarks and exhibit specimens where possible.
